questions.q: What is Personally Identifiable Information (PII)?
options: Any data collected by a website
Information that can be used to identify an individual
Encrypted passwords only
Publicly available corporate data

questions.q: Which of these is considered a best practice for password security?
options: Using the same password for all accounts
Writing passwords on sticky notes
Using a password manager and enabling 2FA
Using your birthdate as a password

questions.q: What does Phishing mean in cybersecurity?
options: A technique to catch fish using technology
A fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive information by disguising as a trustworthy entity
Scanning a network for vulnerabilities
Encrypting data to prevent access

questions.q: What is a cookie in web browsers?
options: A small piece of data stored on the user's computer to remember state and session info
A virus that steals credentials
A script that runs background cryptocurrency mining
A protocol for secure database connections

questions.q: Why is oversharing on social media a major privacy risk?
options: It increases browser page load times
It violates social platform terms of service
It provides attackers with personal details for social engineering or security question answers
It automatically deletes previous posts

questions.q: What does GDPR stand for?
options: General Data Protection Regulation
Global Data Privacy Rules
General Digital Privacy Requirements
Global Digital Protection Rights

questions.q: Under GDPR, what is the 'Right to be Forgotten'?
options: The right to forget your passwords
The right to have your personal data erased by an organization
The right to opt-out of marketing emails
The right to browse anonymously

questions.q: What is the maximum fine for a severe GDPR violation?
options: Up to €10,000 or 1% global turnover
Up to €500,000 flat rate
Up to €20 Million or 4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher
GDPR only issues warnings, not financial fines

questions.q: Under GDPR, within how many hours must a data breach be reported to supervisory authorities?
options: 24 hours
72 hours
7 days
30 days

questions.q: Which principle of GDPR states that data collected should be limited only to what is necessary?
options: Integrity and confidentiality
Storage limitation
Data Minimization
Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency

questions.q: What is Federated Learning?
options: Training a model on a centralized server
Training an algorithm across multiple decentralized edge devices without exchanging raw data samples
A method to combine different AI models
Learning using federal government datasets

questions.q: How does Differential Privacy work?
options: By encrypting all database records
By hiding the IP address of users
By adding statistical noise to datasets to prevent identification of individuals in query results
By completely removing all PII from the database

questions.q: What is Homomorphic Encryption?
options: A method to encrypt homepage files in a web server
A form of encryption that allows mathematical operations on ciphertexts, producing encrypted results
A multi-layered password hashing technique
An encryption protocol reserved strictly for military communications

questions.q: In machine learning security, what is a 'Model Inversion Attack'?
options: An attack where the adversary reconstructs original training data using model predictions
Flipping the neural network architecture upside down to crash servers
Injecting malicious inputs to cause misclassification
Stealing the weights of a commercial AI model

questions.q: What is 'Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Data'?
options: An exact copy of real data with names changed to generic templates
Artificial data generated from real data that maintains mathematical relationships without exposing real individual records
Encrypted data arrays that cannot be read without a private key
Publicly available census datasets

questions.q: What is a Ransomware attack?
options: Malware that secretly records browser activity
Malware that encrypts files and demands financial payment to restore access
A DDoS attack on domain name servers
An attack targeting physical routers

questions.q: What does 2FA stand for and what is its goal?
options: Two-Factor Authentication; adding an extra layer of security beyond passwords
Double File Allocation; ensuring file system redundancy
Two-Fold Access; allowing two simultaneous logins
Dual Firewall Architecture; running two network security systems

questions.q: What is a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack?
options: An attack targeting the middle layer of a database schema
When an attacker secretly intercepts and alters communication between two parties
A physical breach of server server-rooms
An inside developer injecting malicious code

questions.q: What is spyware?
options: Software designed to debug complex API integrations
A browser extension that acts as a proxy
Malicious software that secretly records user keystrokes and data and sends it to third parties
An automated script that crawls public search engines

questions.q: What is a Zero-Day vulnerability?
options: A security flaw that has been patched for exactly one year
A flaw discovered on the first day of a month
A software security flaw that is unknown to the vendor and has no patch available
An account password that expires within 24 hours

questions.q: What is algorithmic bias in machine learning?
options: Systematic, repeatable errors in AI outcomes that create unfair treatment of certain groups
An intentional feature added to speed up neural networks
A hardware error caused by CPU thermal throttling
When an AI model achieves 100% test accuracy

questions.q: What is Explainable AI (XAI)?
options: A dictionary defining all technical terms used in AI documents
A set of methods that allows human users to comprehend and trust AI predictions and decisions
An AI model that automatically writes code documentation
A search engine for artificial intelligence papers

questions.q: Which of these is a primary cause of bias in AI systems?
options: Using modern GPU clusters
Training models using too many variables
Historical biases and structural inequalities reflected in training datasets
Encrypting user data prior to training

questions.q: What does the 'Right to Explanation' under GDPR mean for users?
options: Users must explain why they want their accounts deleted
The right to obtain meaningful information about the logic and consequences of automated decision-making
Developers must explain how they wrote the software code
Companies must explain their general server architecture to the public

questions.q: In Responsible AI, what does 'Data Lineage' refer to?
options: A diagram of parent-child relationships in a SQL database
The chronological history of data, showing its origins, transformations, and where it is consumed
The size of a database backups list
A legal contract signed between data providers

questions.q: What is the critical first action an organization should take upon discovering a data breach?
options: Immediately issue a press release
Contain the breach to prevent further exposure and secure network systems
Delete the affected database tables
Sue the software vendors

questions.q: In breach response, what does 'Triage' mean?
options: Restoring database tables from older tapes
Assessing and prioritizing the severity, scope, and potential impact of the breach
Running three parallel security audits
Creating three backup system accounts

questions.q: Why is transparent communication with affected users important after a breach?
options: It speeds up website loading times
It helps users protect their accounts (e.g. change passwords) and maintains organization credibility
It allows companies to avoid paying fines entirely
It increases sales of cybersecurity packages

questions.q: What is a 'Post-Mortem' in incident response?
options: A backup server running secondary tasks
An analysis conducted after the breach is resolved to identify root causes and improve security controls
Deleting credentials of former employees
A forensic analysis of physical locks

questions.q: What is a 'Credential Stuffing' attack?
options: Filling form fields with arbitrary letters to crash websites
An automated cyberattack where lists of compromised username/password pairs are tested against other websites
When an administrator forgets their security keys
A method of storing cleartext passwords in databases
